subtitle: Encrypt phones, computers, drives and folders.

subsections.title: Encrypt Your Devices
subsections.summary: Lock everything on a lost or stolen device.

blocks.html: Full-disk encryption means a thief or anyone who seizes your device gets scrambled data, not your files. Most devices can do it with a setting.

items.title: iPhone & iPad
items.text: Encrypted automatically as soon as you set a passcode. Use a long alphanumeric passcode rather than six digits.

items.title: Android
items.text: Android 10 and newer encrypt by default. Check under Settings → Security → Encryption & credentials (names vary by phone), and use a strong screen lock.

items.title: Mac
items.text: System Settings → Privacy & Security → FileVault → Turn On. Keep the recovery key in your password manager, not in iCloud if you want Apple out of the loop.

items.title: Windows
items.text: BitLocker on Windows 10/11 Pro, Enterprise or Education (Settings → Privacy & security → Device encryption or BitLocker). Add a start-up PIN for extra protection. Home editions can use VeraCrypt system encryption instead.

items.title: Linux
items.text: Full-disk encryption is chosen during installation (“Encrypt the new installation” / LUKS). On an existing system that means backing up and reinstalling.

blocks.label: Shut down, don’t sleep
blocks.html: Encryption only protects a device that is fully powered off. Before crossing a border, going to a protest or leaving a laptop unattended, shut it down.

subsections.title: Encrypt Drives & Files
subsections.summary: USB drives, external disks and sensitive folders.

blocks.html: External drives get lost and seized more often than laptops. Encrypt the whole drive — macOS Disk Utility (format as “encrypted”), BitLocker To Go on Windows, or VeraCrypt on any computer — or keep sensitive files in an encrypted vault.

items.label: VeraCrypt
items.desc: Encrypts whole drives, partitions or file containers. Can hide a second volume behind a decoy password.

items.label: Cryptomator
items.desc: Encrypts a folder file by file — ideal for anything you keep in a cloud.

items.label: Tails
items.desc: A system that runs from a USB stick, leaves no trace and can keep an encrypted persistent folder.

items.label: Tella
items.desc: Hides and encrypts photos, video and audio — built for documenting abuses.

items.text: Lock (unmount) vaults when you step away, before sleep, and before handing over a device
Eject drives in the system before unplugging them
items.details: Pulling a drive out while it’s open can corrupt files.

items.text: Never open an encrypted vault on a computer you don’t trust
items.details: Malware can record your password as you type it.

items.text: Use a long, unique password and store it in your password manager
items.details: See Passwords. There is no “forgot password” for encryption.

items.text: Buy and repair devices through people you trust
items.details: Have second-hand devices wiped and checked before use.
